title: Синие киты и второй ребёнок  (Blue Whales and a Second Child)

segments.t: At home in bed, Nastya tells her husband Kostya about a television documentary she watched on blue whales. When Kostya misses her subtle hint about family size, Nastya comes right out and asks to have a second baby. Let's listen to their bedtime conversation in Russian.
Сегодня была программа про синих китов.
Мне их стало так жалко.
Они остаются друг с другом навсегда.
Это же правда очень мило.
Но этих китов сейчас очень мало.
Костя тебя внимательно слышал, дорогая.
Может, нам второго ребёнка завести?
Настя, но мы же не киты.
У нас уже есть один сын.
Надо будет — потом ещё сделаем.
У тебя всё так просто получается!
А обо мне ты вообще подумал?
Now let's break down Nastya and Kostya's debate about a second child line by line.
Сегодня была программа про синих китов.
'Today there was a program about blue whales.' The preposition meaning about governs the animate accusative plural of blue whales, which matches the genitive.
Мне их стало так жалко.
'I felt so sorry for them.' An impersonal dative construction with a predicate adverb expresses pity for someone.
Они остаются друг с другом навсегда.
'They stay with each other forever.' The reciprocal pronoun phrase meaning with one another takes the instrumental case.
Это же правда очень мило.
'That really is very sweet.' Nastya sighs romantically using a neuter short predicate adjective meaning sweet or cute.
Но этих китов сейчас очень мало.
'But there are very few of these whales right now.' A quantifier meaning few or little governs the genitive plural of these whales.
Костя тебя внимательно слышал, дорогая.
'Kostya heard you carefully, dear.' Half-reading his magazine, Kostya insists that he was paying attention to her story.
Может, нам второго ребёнка завести?
'Maybe we should have a second child?' A dative plural pronoun with a perfective infinitive proposes having another baby.
Настя, но мы же не киты.
'Nastya, we are not whales, after all.' Kostya tries to dodge the topic with a joke using a nominative plural noun.
У нас уже есть один сын.
'We already have one son.' He reminds her that they are already raising their young son Styopa.
Надо будет — потом ещё сделаем.
'If we need to, we will have another one later.' Kostya brushes the question off casually with an impersonal future condition.
У тебя всё так просто получается!
'Everything is so simple with you!' Nastya bristles at his carefree tone using a possessive phrase and adverb.
А обо мне ты вообще подумал?

'And did you think about me at all?' Before the prepositional pronoun me, the preposition meaning about expands to its two-syllable form. Let's hear the bedroom conversation between Nastya and Kostya from start to finish.

Offended by Kostya's casual attitude toward having another baby, Nastya turns her back on him in bed. Listen for the plural noun meaning whales and the ordinal numeral meaning second. See you in the next scene.
